chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Do not anoint yourself with oil containing musk or amber when you intend to enter the state of Ihram, for the sake of the scent that remains in your head after you have entered Ihram; and anoint yourself with whatever oil you wish when you intend to enter Ihram. So when you enter Ihram, the oil becomes prohibited for you until you are released (from Ihram).

key_terms.إحرام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تحل: To be released or freed (from the state of Ihram)

ai.seo_question: Can I use perfumed oil before entering Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between the permissibility of using scented oils for enjoyment prior to Ihram and their prohibition once the state is entered, emphasizing that the scent itself does not invalidate the ritual. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that the prohibition applies to the substance applied to the body during Ihram, ensuring the pilgrim remains in a state of ritual purity and simplicity. This ruling underscores the importance of intention and the specific conditions of the Hajj rites as derived from the Imams.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘You should not massage with oil when you intend to wear Ihraam, with oil in which is Musk or Amber, due to the reason of its aroma remaining in your head after having worn Ihraam; and you can massage with whatever you so desire to from the oils, when you intend to wear Ihraam. So when you wear Ihraam, then the oil becomes Prohibited unto you until you are free (from Ihraam)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

You must not apply any oil which has musk or ambergris; for its perfume remains in your head after Ihram. You can apply oil when you want to assume the state of Ihram, once you are in the state of Ihram; applying becomes unlawful until you come out of the state of Ihram.’”
